title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 30 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 30 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 30 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 30.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 30, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Hezekiah sent letters to Ephraim and Manasseh
King and princes took counsel to keep the passover in the second month
A decree was established to proclaim keeping the passover throughout Israel
Posts went with letters from the king throughout Israel and Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah sent letters to Ephraim and Manasseh
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sending letters to Ephraim and Manasseh to come to the house of the LORD at Jerusalem is the first event mentioned in 2 Chronicles 30:1.

questions.question: Who did Hezekiah send letters to, asking them to come to Jerusalem to keep the passover?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephraim and Manasseh
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sent letters to Ephraim and Manasseh to come to Jerusalem to keep the passover, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:1.

questions.question: When did the king, princes, and congregation decide to keep the passover?
questions.correctAnswer: In the second month
questions.explanation: The king, princes, and congregation took counsel to keep the passover in the second month according to 2 Chronicles 30:2.

questions.question: Why could they not keep the passover at the usual time?
options: Because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently
Because there was no king in Jerusalem
Because the people were in captivity
questions.correctAnswer: Because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently
questions.explanation: They could not keep the passover at the usual time because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:3.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the king and all the congregation to the plan to keep the passover in the second month?
questions.correctAnswer: They were pleased
questions.explanation: The plan to keep the passover in the second month pleased the king and all the congregation, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:4.

questions.question: From where to where was the decree to proclaim the keeping of the passover made?
questions.correctAnswer: From Beersheba to Dan
questions.explanation: The decree was proclaimed throughout all Israel from Beersheba even to Dan, according to 2 Chronicles 30:5.

questions.question: What was the reason given for proclaiming the keeping of the passover in such a manner?
options: Because they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written
Because the king wanted to show his power
Because the priests insisted on it
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written
questions.explanation: The proclamation was made because they had not kept the passover in such a way for a long time, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:5.

questions.question: What did the king’s letters command the children of Israel to do?
options: Turn again unto the LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel
Build a new temple in Jerusalem
Offer sacrifices in their own cities
questions.correctAnswer: Turn again unto the LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel
questions.explanation: The king's letters commanded the children of Israel to turn again unto the LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, as found in 2 Chronicles 30:6.

questions.question: What warning did the king give about being like their fathers and brethren?
options: Not to trespass against the LORD God of their fathers
questions.correctAnswer: Not to trespass against the LORD God of their fathers
questions.explanation: The king warned not to be like their fathers who trespassed against the LORD God of their fathers, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:7.

questions.question: How did the king describe the sanctuary to which the people should yield themselves?
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctified forever
questions.explanation: The king said the sanctuary was sanctified forever, as found in 2 Chronicles 30:8.

questions.question: What is promised if the people turn again unto the LORD according to the king’s message?
options: Their brethren and children will find compassion and return to the land
They will gain riches and honor
Their enemies will be destroyed immediately
They will never face captivity again
questions.correctAnswer: Their brethren and children will find compassion and return to the land
questions.explanation: If they turn again unto the LORD, their brethren and children shall find compassion and come again into the land, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:9.

questions.question: Hezekiah sent letters to all Israel and Judah to keep the passover at the house of the LORD at Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sent letters to all Israel and Judah to come to the house of the LORD at Jerusalem to keep the passover, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:1.

questions.question: The king and all the congregation were pleased with the plan to keep the passover in the second month.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The plan to keep the passover in the second month pleased the king and all the congregation, according to 2 Chronicles 30:4.

questions.question: The text says the people gathered themselves together to Jerusalem at the usual time of the passover.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text states they could not keep it at the usual time because the people had not gathered themselves together to Jerusalem, as in 2 Chronicles 30:3.

questions.question: The chapter states that the king commanded the people to fight the kings of Assyria.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not command fighting the kings of Assyria; rather, it calls for turning to the LORD for deliverance, as in 2 Chronicles 30:6.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 30 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 30 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the people of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Zebulun do when they received the posts about the Passover?
options: They sent gifts to the king
questions.correctAnswer: They laughed and mocked them
questions.explanation: The people laughed them to scorn and mocked them as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:10.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 30:11 indicate about some people of Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun?
options: They humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem
They were angry with the king
questions.correctAnswer: They humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: This verse indicates that despite the mockery, some humbled themselves and responded positively by coming to Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:11.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the assembly in Jerusalem mentioned in 2 Chronicles 30:13?
options: To keep the feast of unleavened bread
questions.correctAnswer: To keep the feast of unleavened bread
questions.explanation: The assembly was convened to keep the feast of unleavened bread as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 30:13.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 30:14, what actions did the people take regarding the altars in Jerusalem?
options: They took away the altars and cast them into the brook Kidron
questions.correctAnswer: They took away the altars and cast them into the brook Kidron
questions.explanation: This verse describes how the people arose, took away the altars, and cast them into the brook Kidron, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:14.

questions.question: What did the priests and Levites do when they killed the Passover according to 2 Chronicles 30:15?
options: They were ashamed and sanctified themselves
They called for more people to join
questions.correctAnswer: They were ashamed and sanctified themselves
questions.explanation: The priests and Levites felt ashamed and sanctified themselves as they prepared to kill the Passover, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 30:15.

questions.question: In what manner did the priests stand according to 2 Chronicles 30:16?
options: According to the law of Moses
In a circle around the altar
questions.correctAnswer: According to the law of Moses
questions.explanation: The priests stood in their place according to the law of Moses, indicating their obedience to God's commands, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:16.

questions.question: What challenge did the Levites face in 2 Chronicles 30:17?
options: They had to find more animals
They had the charge of the killing of the Passovers for those not sanctified
They were overwhelmed by the crowd
questions.correctAnswer: They had the charge of the killing of the Passovers for those not sanctified
questions.explanation: This verse states that the Levites were tasked with the responsibility of killing the Passovers for those who were not sanctified, highlighting their role in maintaining holiness, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:17.

questions.question: What was Hezekiah's prayer for the multitude who had not cleansed themselves as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 30:18?
options: That they would not eat the Passover
questions.correctAnswer: That they would be forgiven
questions.explanation: Hezekiah prayed for them saying that the good LORD pardon everyone, showing his desire for their forgiveness, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:18.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 30:5 reveal about the frequency of the Passover celebration?
options: They had not done it in a long time
It was only for the priests
questions.correctAnswer: They had not done it in a long time
questions.explanation: This verse indicates that the Passover had not been celebrated in such a manner for a long time, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:5.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 30:9 promise if the people turn again unto the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall find compassion
questions.explanation: The verse promises that if they turn back to the LORD, their brethren and children shall find compassion, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:9.

questions.question: What attitude does 2 Chronicles 30:8 encourage the people to adopt?
questions.correctAnswer: Yield themselves to the LORD
questions.explanation: This verse encourages the people not to be stiffnecked but to yield themselves to the LORD, emphasizing obedience and submission, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:8.

questions.question: The actions of the people in 2 Chronicles 30:14 indicate a desire to:
questions.correctAnswer: Repent and return to God
questions.explanation: By taking away the altars, the people were showing a desire to turn away from idolatry and return to worshiping God properly, as seen in 2 Chronicles 30:14.

questions.question: Did the Levites have to handle the Passover for those who were not clean according to 2 Chronicles 30:17?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Yes, the Levites were tasked with the charge of the killing of the Passovers for those who were not clean, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:17.

questions.question: The people of Ephraim and Manasseh mocked Hezekiah's proclamation according to 2 Chronicles 30:10.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: They laughed them to scorn and mocked them, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:10.

questions.question: Hezekiah was indifferent to the people's uncleanliness as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 30:18.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hezekiah prayed for them, showing his concern for their uncleanliness and desire for their pardon, as stated in 2 Chronicles 30:18.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 30 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 30.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 30:19, what condition is described for a person seeking God despite not being cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary?
options: That prepareth his heart to seek God
questions.correctAnswer: That prepareth his heart to seek God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:19 states, "That prepareth his heart to seek God, the LORD God of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary." This indicates the condition is preparing one's heart.

questions.question: What was the LORD's response to Hezekiah's prayer for the people in 2 Chronicles 30:20?
options: He hearkened to Hezekiah and healed the people
He sent a prophet to guide them
He allowed the feast to continue
questions.correctAnswer: He hearkened to Hezekiah and healed the people
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:20 says, "And the LORD hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people," showing God's direct response to Hezekiah's prayer.

questions.question: How long did the children of Israel keep the feast of unleavened bread in Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 30:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:21 states, "And the children of Israel that were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness," specifying the duration.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do for the Levites during the feast as described in 2 Chronicles 30:22?
options: Spoke comfortably to them and they ate throughout the feast
Sent them on missions to other cities
Ordered them to fast and pray
Commanded them to build a new altar
questions.correctAnswer: Spoke comfortably to them and they ate throughout the feast
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:22 says, "And Hezekiah spake comfortably unto all the Levites that taught the good knowledge of the LORD: and they did eat throughout the feast seven days," showing Hezekiah's encouragement.

questions.question: How many additional days did the whole assembly decide to keep the feast according to 2 Chronicles 30:23?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:23 states, "And the whole assembly took counsel to keep other seven days: and they kept other seven days with gladness," indicating an extension of the celebration.

questions.question: What substantial offerings did Hezekiah and the princes give to the congregation according to 2 Chronicles 30:24?
options: Hezekiah gave a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep; princes gave a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep
Hezekiah gave five hundred bullocks and two thousand sheep; princes gave one thousand bullocks and five thousand sheep
Hezekiah gave two thousand bullocks and five thousand sheep; princes gave one thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep
Hezekiah gave one hundred bullocks and one thousand sheep; princes gave five hundred bullocks and three thousand sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah gave a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep; princes gave a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:24 records, "For Hezekiah king of Judah did give to the congregation a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep; and the princes gave to the congregation a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep," indicating the magnitude of their offerings.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'hearkened' (שָׁמַע, shamaʿ) in 2 Chronicles 30:20 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To listen attentively and obey
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'שָׁמַע' (shamaʿ) means 'to hear' with the implication of attentive listening and obeying, as used in 2 Chronicles 30:20 where "the LORD hearkened to Hezekiah."

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in 2 Chronicles 30:26 where it says, 'So there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon... there was not the like in Jerusalem'?
questions.correctAnswer: Hyperbole
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:26 uses hyperbole to emphasize the unparalleled joy in Jerusalem since Solomon’s time, exaggerating for effect.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of sincere heart seeking God despite ceremonial impurity found in 2 Chronicles 30:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 10:22
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:22 encourages believers to draw near to God with a true heart in full assurance of faith, paralleling the sincere heart seeking God in 2 Chronicles 30:19.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of restoring proper worship and celebration of Passover as in 2 Chronicles 30:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 9:1-14
questions.explanation: Numbers 9:1-14 describes the observance of Passover including provisions for those unclean or on a journey, which relates to Hezekiah's Passover celebration in 2 Chronicles 30:1-3.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the description of the LORD hearkening to Hezekiah and healing the people in 2 Chronicles 30:20?
options: Hezekiah's prayer for those not cleansed according to purification of the sanctuary
The killing of the Passover lambs on the fourteenth day of the second month
The removal of altars and incense stands in Jerusalem
The sending of letters inviting Israel and Judah to the Passover
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah's prayer for those not cleansed according to purification of the sanctuary
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:19 shows Hezekiah praying for those who had not purified themselves according to the sanctuary, which immediately precedes verse 20 where the LORD hears and heals them.

questions.question: In historical context, what significance did the 'great joy in Jerusalem' described in 2 Chronicles 30:26 have in relation to the kingdom's history?
options: It was the greatest celebration since Solomon’s reign
It marked the beginning of the Babylonian exile
It commemorated the building of the first temple
It was the first Passover celebrated under King David
questions.correctAnswer: It was the greatest celebration since Solomon’s reign
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:26 explicitly states the joy was unparalleled since Solomon, indicating a restoration and renewal after years of neglect and division.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in 2 Chronicles 30:27 when the priests and Levites' voice is described as going up to heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: Personification
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:27 personifies the voice and prayer as ascending to heaven, attributing human action to intangible elements.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 30:25 reflect a typology of inclusive worship in the post-exilic community?
options: It includes Jews, priests, Levites, Israelites, and strangers dwelling in Judah rejoicing together
It focuses only on the priests and Levites without the common people
It describes a solitary king's personal worship
questions.correctAnswer: It includes Jews, priests, Levites, Israelites, and strangers dwelling in Judah rejoicing together
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:25 emphasizes a diverse assembly joyfully worshiping together, a typology for the inclusive worship community after exile.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 30:21, the Levites and priests praised the LORD silently during the feast of unleavened bread.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:21 states the Levites and priests praised the LORD "singing with loud instruments," indicating vocal and instrumental praise, not silence.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 30 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 30 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 30:9 teach about God's nature in relation to repentance and mercy?
options: God is gracious and merciful, willing to forgive those who return to Him
God is indifferent to human repentance once sin is committed
God punishes all sin without exception regardless of repentance
God's mercy is limited to Israel alone and excludes the remnant
questions.correctAnswer: God is gracious and merciful, willing to forgive those who return to Him
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:9 states that the LORD God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away His face if the people return to Him, teaching God's nature as merciful and forgiving upon repentance.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does 2 Chronicles 30:7 teach through the example of Israel's ancestors?
options: Sin leads to desolation as a consequence of trespassing against God
Sin is excusable if committed unknowingly
Human sin does not affect the community or future generations
Sin can be ignored if sacrifices are offered
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to desolation as a consequence of trespassing against God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:7 warns that the fathers and brethren trespassed against the LORD God, which led to desolation, teaching the doctrine that sin brings divine judgment and destruction.

questions.question: What doctrine of sanctification does 2 Chronicles 30:17 teach about the role of the Levites?
options: The Levites are responsible for sanctifying those who are unclean to the LORD
Sanctification is unnecessary for participation in the Passover
Only priests have the authority to sanctify people
Sanctification is a one-time event with no ongoing responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites are responsible for sanctifying those who are unclean to the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states the Levites had the charge of killing the passovers for every one that was not clean, to sanctify them unto the LORD, teaching their role in the process of sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 30:20 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 30:20 shows that the LORD hearkened to Hezekiah and healed the people, demonstrating God's attribute of mercy in responding to prayer and healing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 30:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 8 calls the people to yield themselves to the LORD and enter His sanctuary which He has sanctified forever, highlighting God's holiness as He sanctifies His sanctuary.

questions.question: How does the celebration of the Passover in 2 Chronicles 30 prepare for the Messianic fulfillment in the New Testament?
options: It anticipates Christ as the ultimate Passover Lamb who takes away sin
It focuses solely on national restoration without spiritual implications
It emphasizes legalistic ritual without grace
It rejects the need for future fulfillment in Christ
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Christ as the ultimate Passover Lamb who takes away sin
questions.explanation: The Passover in 2 Chronicles 30 recalls God's deliverance and foreshadows Jesus Christ as the ultimate Passover Lamb (cf. 1 Corinthians 5:7), connecting this feast to redemptive history.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does the invitation in 2 Chronicles 30:6 make regarding Israel's restoration?
options: It echoes the covenant promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel concerning return and restoration
It denies the possibility of any restoration for Israel
It focuses only on political alliances with Assyria
It promotes syncretism with foreign gods
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the covenant promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel concerning return and restoration
questions.explanation: Verse 6 calls Israel to turn to the LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, recalling the covenant promises to the patriarchs and God's faithfulness to restore His people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 30:8 and 2 Chronicles 30:9 teach about human response and divine grace?
options: Human yielding and entering God's sanctuary results in the turning away of divine wrath and reception of mercy
Human effort alone is sufficient for salvation
Divine grace is unconditional regardless of human response
God's wrath cannot be turned away by human actions
questions.correctAnswer: Human yielding and entering God's sanctuary results in the turning away of divine wrath and reception of mercy
questions.explanation: Verse 8 urges yielding to God and entering His sanctified sanctuary to turn away wrath, while verse 9 promises God's grace and mercy to those who return, teaching the cooperation of human repentance and divine mercy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 30:17 and 2 Chronicles 30:18 teach about sanctification and prayer for the imperfect?
options: Though many were not properly sanctified, prayer and divine forgiveness allow their participation in the Passover
Only those fully sanctified can be accepted, and prayer cannot compensate
Participation without sanctification is a sin without remedy
questions.correctAnswer: Though many were not properly sanctified, prayer and divine forgiveness allow their participation in the Passover
questions.explanation: Verse 17 notes many were unclean but the Levites sanctified them, and verse 18 records Hezekiah's prayer for those imperfectly cleansed, showing God's acceptance through prayer and sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 30:14 and 2 Chronicles 30:15 teach about proper worship and the rejection of idolatry?
options: True worship requires removing false altars and observing the Passover according to the law
Idolatry is tolerated alongside true worship
Altars and incense have no significance in worship
The timing of Passover is unimportant
questions.correctAnswer: True worship requires removing false altars and observing the Passover according to the law
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes removing altars and incense that were improper, and verse 15 shows killing the Passover on the appointed day, teaching the necessity of pure worship in accordance with God's commands.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the people who participated in the Passover without proper cleansing were hypocrites and their worship was rejected. What does 2 Chronicles 30:17-20 actually teach?
options: God accepted the imperfect who sincerely sought Him, as Hezekiah prayed and God healed the people
Only perfectly cleansed people could participate and be accepted
The Passover was invalidated by improper sanctification
Hezekiah ignored the law and God condemned the people
questions.correctAnswer: God accepted the imperfect who sincerely sought Him, as Hezekiah prayed and God healed the people
questions.explanation: Verses 17-20 show many were not cleansed, but Hezekiah prayed for them, and God heard and healed the people, teaching God's acceptance of sincere seekers despite imperfect ritual purity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 30:13 teach about corporate worship and communal sanctification?
options: A large congregation gathered to observe the feast in unity, demonstrating the importance of corporate worship
Individual worship is superior to corporate gatherings
Sanctification is a purely private matter
Communal worship is unnecessary if the heart is right
questions.correctAnswer: A large congregation gathered to observe the feast in unity, demonstrating the importance of corporate worship
questions.explanation: Verse 13 describes a very great congregation assembled to keep the feast, emphasizing the biblical doctrine of corporate worship and communal sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 30:12 specifically demonstrate in relation to the people's unified response?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that the hand of God was to give them one heart to obey the king and princes by His word, showing God’s sovereign power over human hearts.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 30:21 and 2 Chronicles 30:27 teach about worship and prayer in the life of the community?
options: Joyful worship with music and the priests’ blessing demonstrate communal praise and the efficacy of prayer
Worship should be silent and without music
Blessings by priests are unnecessary and ineffective
Prayer has no effect on God's dwelling
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful worship with music and the priests’ blessing demonstrate communal praise and the efficacy of prayer
questions.explanation: Verse 21 describes praise with loud instruments and verse 27 tells of the priests blessing the people with their prayers ascending to heaven, teaching the biblical doctrine of joyful worship and effective prayer.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 30:24 theologically underscore the role of leadership in corporate worship and sacrifice?
options: King Hezekiah and princes provided abundant offerings, modeling generous leadership in worship
Leaders were absent from worship responsibilities
Leadership restricted the participation of the common people
Only priests were responsible for offerings
questions.correctAnswer: King Hezekiah and princes provided abundant offerings, modeling generous leadership in worship
questions.explanation: Verse 24 records Hezekiah and the princes giving large numbers of animals for sacrifice, teaching the doctrine that godly leadership involves generous provision for corporate worship.
